_doc: THE OPEN-PR HANDOFF RECORD. What a manager arriving COLD needs to know about every
PR in flight that it did not open -- and what the operator DECIDED about every PR
that has since settled.
WHY IT EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-02T06:17Z while checking whether a manager handoff
would actually work: SESSIONS.json carried ZERO structured PR fields and 19 rows
mentioning a PR only in PROSE, and nothing anywhere mapped a PR to its owning
session, its blocker, or the operator decisions already attached to it. A cold
manager would have had to grep prose.
⚠️ THE DANGEROUS CASE IS NOT A FORGOTTEN PR -- IT IS A FORGOTTEN APPROVAL.
#10746 carries a Tier-2 operator approval that is CONDITIONAL (stage on bybit_1,
NOT a fleet-wide flip). A manager that does not know the approval exists stalls and
re-asks, which is merely wasteful. A manager that knows it was approved but NOT the
condition could merge it fleet-wide onto a real-money account. Those are opposite
failure modes and only the second is dangerous, which is why `operator_decision`
records the CONDITION and not just the verdict.
⚠️ TWO POPULATIONS AS OF schema_version 3 (MI-57). READ WHICH ONE YOU ARE IN.
open_prs[]    an IN-FLIGHT CLAIM -- this PR is open, here is its owner and its
blocker. GRADED against a live observation of what is open, and
legitimately stale the moment the PR merges.
settled_prs[] the DURABLE DECISION RECORD -- what the operator said about #X,
verbatim. HISTORY. It is *more* load-bearing after the merge than
before it, and it is NEVER compared to the live open list.
⚠️ PRUNING IS A MOVE, NOT A DELETE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT.
Until MI-57 both populations shared one key, so the only way to satisfy the
freshness rule was to DELETE the row -- taking the operator decision with it. Eight
rows were destroyed that way on 2026-09-02 (see settled_prs[], each carrying
`operator_decision_not_preserved: true`). That is the same shape as the OPEN-ITEMS
cap that instructed a session to EVICT a valid row to satisfy a rule nothing was
checking -- CLAUDE.md § 'Every session' records it. A record that destroys knowledge
to look current is worse than one that looks stale.
⚠️ THE OLD _doc SAID THIS FILE 'GOES STALE THE MOMENT A PR MERGES'. THAT IS NO
LONGER THE SHAPE and the sentence has been removed rather than left standing.
A settled row is moved to settled_prs[] by scripts/ops/reconcile_open_prs.py, which
runs on `push: main` -- OUTSIDE the commit being merged, because a commit cannot
record its own merge. That was the terminator for the regress this file used to
declare structural and unfixable. It also said 'MI-43 is building the check'; MI-43
shipped, so that is gone too. (Field beats comment: fix the stale text, never flip
the field on inference.)
⚠️ GITHUB IS STILL THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR PR STATE. Read this file for OWNERSHIP,
INTENT and DECISIONS, which GitHub does not carry; re-read CI and mergeability from
the API before acting on any row. `as_of` is when a human last touched it.
⚠️ `last_reconciled_sha` IS STAMPED ONLY ON A MOVE, DELIBERATELY. A no-op pass
writes nothing -- a liveness stamp would be a commit to main, which retriggers the
reconciler, which stamps again. If a row here names a PR that is no longer open AND
this sha lags main, the RECONCILER IS NOT RUNNING; that is a different finding from
'a session forgot to prune' and open_pr_record.py reports it as one. Do not prune by
hand to clear it -- that hides the dead automation.
⚠️ `operator_decision` IS A TYPED OBJECT AS OF MI-43, NOT A STRING.
{verdict, condition, scope, decided_on, text}. `verdict` is a closed vocabulary --
approved | approved_with_conditions | not_required | pending | none_recorded --
and `text` MUST carry the operator's original wording VERBATIM so the typed verdict
stays checkable against what was actually said. scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py
--strict FAILS a row whose verdict is `approved_with_conditions` while recording
neither `condition` nor `scope`: that row reads as approved, which is the
half-informed state that could merge a demo-only approval onto a real-money account.
⚠️ A SETTLED ROW HAS ITS OWN FAILING CHECK, so the split did not remove the teeth.
`terminal` is merged | closed_unmerged | unknown_not_reconstructible, and a row that
did NOT reach main with no `disposition` FAILS --strict. An abandoned PR with no
stated reason is real lost knowledge: 'superseded by #X', 'the operator refused it'
and 'the author gave up' imply opposite next actions and an undispositioned row
cannot tell them apart. The reconciler may never write
`unknown_not_reconstructible` -- it either observed a terminal or it could_not_look
and moved nothing.
⚠️ WHAT THAT DOES **NOT** CATCH, SAID PLAINLY: an author who writes
`verdict: approved` where the operator actually attached conditions. Nothing inside
the repo can detect that -- knowing a condition was given requires knowing what the
operator said, and THIS FILE IS THAT RECORD. The typed form narrows the failure from
'a condition silently absent from prose nobody parses' to 'a verdict field a reader
can compare against `text`'. A narrowing, not a closure.
maintained_by: the manager session holding the lease; settled_prs[] is maintained by scripts/ops/reconcile_open_prs.py
source_of_truth_note: GitHub is authoritative for state; this file is authoritative for ownership, intent and operator decisions.
last_reconciled_note: null because the reconciler has never run -- it ships in this change. This is NOT 'nothing has ever settled': the eight settled_prs[] rows were migrated by hand from the destructive prune that preceded it. A null here with stale rows in open_prs[] reads as `reconciler_not_run`, which is the correct reading until the first post-merge run stamps it.

⚠️_manager_is_github_write_rate_limited: CLEARED 2026-09-02T07:5xZ — write calls (update_pull_request, merge_pull_request, issue_write, create_pull_request) all succeeded again. The limit was self-inflicted: polling get_check_runs in a loop across ~11 PRs for hours. #10757 (the CI waiter, now MERGED as 066bfa7f) is the mechanism that removes that waste — use it instead of polling.
⚠️_a_row_can_UNDER_claim_and_no_check_ca: Found 2026-09-02 on this very row. `open_pr_record.py --strict` grades a verdict that DECLARES conditions and records none — the over-claiming direction, which is the dangerous one. It cannot catch the OPPOSITE: I typed #10758 `none_recorded` while a full operator decision, with its condition, sat in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json under MI-34 the whole time. `none_recorded` is a valid verdict needing no condition, so the row passed every check while being simply wrong. ⚠️ The cost is real but is NOT symmetric with the over-claiming case: a successor reading `none_recorded` re-asks the operator — wasteful and SAFE — where one reading a bare 'approved' could merge a demo-only Tier-2 approval onto a real-money account. So this is worth KNOWING, not worth a new failing check: cross-checking every row against the checklist would fire on the many PRs that legitimately have no decision anywhere. The mitigation is the reviewer's, not the guard's — read MANAGER-CHECKLIST for the PR's item before typing `none_recorded`.
⚠️_the_regress_that_used_to_live_here_an: This key REPLACES `⚠️_the_last_row_is_always_stale_and_that_is_STRUCTURAL`, which declared the regress a PROPERTY of the design that terminates 'only if the manager stops opening PRs'. That was an accurate description of the OLD shape and is no longer true, so it is corrected rather than left standing. The regress: every open PR needs a row; the PR that prunes the last stale row is itself an open PR and needs one; merging it makes THAT row stale. Observed live -- #10775 merged (d08cac48) about ninety seconds after a branch recorded a row for it. TWO root causes, and only fixing both terminates it: (1) two populations under one key, so pruning destroyed the decision record -- fixed by settled_prs[]; (2) a commit cannot record its own merge -- fixed by running the reconciler on `push: main`, outside the commit. ⚠️ THE OLD KEY'S WARNING STILL STANDS AND WAS NOT THE THING FIXED: do NOT exempt the currently-merging PR from the completeness check. That exemption is byte-indistinguishable from the real failure the check exists to catch (a PR nobody recorded), and nothing in MI-57 does it -- an open PR with no row still FAILS.
⚠️_the_reconciler_lands_through_an_autom: STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. `main` is branch-protected and REJECTS a direct workflow push (GH006, BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE), so the reconciler lands via .github/actions/commit-to-main, which opens a short-lived automation PR. That PR is an open PR with no row, so `open_prs` reads `unrecorded` for the ~15 minutes it is open. ⚠️ THIS IS A RESIDUAL, NOT A CLOSURE -- but unlike the old regress it TERMINATES: the reconciler commits only when a row actually moved, so the run triggered by its own merge grades `no_change` and opens nothing. One bounded hop, not a loop. It is also not new to this change -- every commit-to-main caller has the same shape, and #10398 and #10781 are automation PRs carrying hand-written rows today.
